optionalSupplies: Towel for damp legs and paws
substitutes: No stream nearby? Use the gutter version after rain, or a quiet canal towpath wide enough to keep well back from the edge.
title: The River Explorer Expedition
clue: Every river starts somewhere ordinary. Today you are going to find out where.
reveal: Follow a brook, canal or even a rain-rivulet upstream with the leash on and the water at a safe distance, to see where it begins. You will probably not find a spring, and that is the point: you will find your furthest point and walk home with the flow.
objective: Follow a calm watercourse upstream on a path, set a turnaround in advance, declare your Furthest Point, and walk home downstream.
instructions: The day before, find your water: a brook, a canal towpath, a drainage stream or, after rain, a trickle running down a street gutter. Check you can walk beside it on a proper path or sidewalk, with railings or a good verge between you and the edge.

Write the turnaround rule on a card before you leave: the time you turn back, or the bridge, gate or bench you stop at. A turnaround you set at home is the one you will keep. Pack the leash, your dog's own bowl and water.

Start at the point where you first reach the water and face upstream. Say what an explorer says: "We are going to find where it begins." Walk on the path side, keeping a body's length or more from the edge.

Let your dog read the path and the bank grass at their own pace. Name the landmarks you pass like a real expedition: the Bridge of Echoes, the Weir, the Big Pipe, the Willow Camp. The water is the guide, and the dog's nose is the scout.
Each time the stream splits or a pipe joins it, stop. Offer your dog the choice of which branch to follow if both are safe and on a path. If only one is safe, say so: "The Tributary That Never Was."
At the turnaround, stop and declare it your Furthest Point whether or not the source appears. Give your dog fresh water from your own bottle, never from the stream, and sit if you can.

Walk home with the current. At the door, pour fresh water into the bowl and say where the water starts, as far as you got. The source is somewhere past the Furthest Point, and that is as good as an unfinished map.
twist: You may never find the source, and that is fine: the Furthest Point counts in full, and the walk home is downstream.
variations: Gutter Upstream, no stream needed: after rain, follow a street gutter's trickle uphill to its start. Keep your dog from drinking it; road runoff can carry oil, salt and chemicals.

Waterhole Walk, for warm (not hot) evenings: choose two or three shaded places near home and bring your own fresh water. Walk between them, pour a little into your dog's bowl at each, and name the longest linger the best waterhole.
Short Stretch for a senior or slow dog: one bridge's length along the bank, a bench, and back. One bridge is a whole river.
Bigger version, optional: a calm stretch of stream or canal with a clear path that you can walk to, if you know it is safe. The nearest water remains the real adventure.
completion: You have reached your turnaround, named the Furthest Point and walked home with the water. Turning round early because your dog is done counts in full.
photoIdea: The water curving away upstream with your dog at the Furthest Point, nose busy on the bank grass. Keep the shot away from the edge.
memoryPrompt: Where did the water seem to start, and what was the most ordinary thing along it?
supplies: Card and a pen for the turnaround rule
safety: Sidewalk too hot for the back of your hand is too hot for paws; head home if your dog pants hard or shivers.
Stay on the path and out of the water; avoid still, foamy or scummy water, and skip it after heavy rain.
Use a short leash (no long line) well back from the edge, and give water from your own bottle, not the stream.
